After every merge, JSON-parse touched bundles, run the typecheck and the production build, and run makemigrations --check / showmigrations for every app with migrations before commit or deploy; resolve mid-object conflicts by re-inserting the added block into one side, never by concatenating both
Reserve the next version value centrally before dispatch or serialize those tickets
Lane 0: generate FE client types from the API schema, or add a code/field parity test, before lanes start adding to the contract
Merge the base branch into the integration branch every wave and re-run every lane's scoped tests on the merged tree; record spec deviations in the spec as they happen

FS-40.name: Invariant enforced in app code without a lock or DB constraint
FS-40.mechanism: Uniqueness, single-row, idempotency and state-transition invariants are enforced by check-then-act in Python (exists() then insert, delete+create, get_or_create/get on non-unique fields, time-window undo, whole-instance save()) without select_for_update, a DB constraint or update_fields. Serial tests pass; concurrent requests, retries, multiple workers or dirty shared DBs break the invariant. In multi-lane builds the lock order is assembled per lane and the harness checks only the first acquisition per kind, so hidden locks (FK KEY SHARE on a FOR UPDATE parent, unique-insert waits, late DELETEs, counter rows, helper-internal locks, re-locks of an earlier tier) deadlock, and each local deadlock fix introduces the next.
trigger_signals: an exists()/get() check followed by an insert, especially with external I/O in between
a worker/outbox table polled by more than one process, or a retryable create-then-persist
save() on a model whose other fields are written asynchronously
get_or_create or .get() on fields with no UniqueConstraint; new automatic assignment of a relation
update_or_create/get_or_create keyed on one FK shared by two source types; an M2M modelling a single-owner relation; a timeout/reaper that mutates status after killing work
a plan where several lanes add locked write paths to one subsystem, or a fix that adds a lock on an earlier-tier resource late in a transaction

a transaction that also takes hidden locks: FK KEY SHARE checks against a parent held FOR UPDATE, unique-key INSERT waits, DELETE row locks late in the transaction, counter/sequence rows (max+1), row locks inside settle/refresh helpers, advisory locks, a re-lock of an earlier tier after a deeper one
a threaded race/deadlock test with barrier or event park points, or a race test that asserts only 'no exception'
a deadlock fix, or a lock-harness finding answered by broadening lock scope; rows read before the lock is held and written back after
preventive_checks: Back the invariant with a DB constraint and catch IntegrityError to return 400 or an idempotent 200
Use select_for_update (skip_locked for workers) on the anchor row and save(update_fields=[...])
Write a two-concurrent-request or kill-between-steps test, and run seeds twice

Lane 0, before parallel lanes start: enumerate EVERY lockable resource of the subsystem (explicit row locks, FK KEY SHARE checks on locked parents, unique-key insert waits, DELETE row locks, counter/sequence rows, locks inside helper functions, advisory locks) into one global order table that every brief cites

Build the lock-order harness once in lane 0: it records EVERY acquisition, not just the first per kind, flags any re-lock of an earlier tier after a deeper one, and runs inside every lane's scoped tests

Ship a threaded deadlock/race test template in lane 0: two real threads (TransactionTestCase), park point placed BEFORE the lock under test, assert end-state consistency (no lost update, no stranded row), and confirm it fails with the lock removed

Run every deadlock fix back through the harness and the threaded tests for EVERY entry point of the subsystem; in this codebase, fixes that reordered one pair or broadened lock scope introduced new deadlocks
Read the rows you will write only after the lock is held; allocate per-parent sequences under a locked counter row or retry on IntegrityError

FS-42.name: Third-party system semantics not honored
FS-42.mechanism: Integrations wrap an external API or platform using the obvious happy-path semantics: single-page list calls, .json() on a 204, a whole status code treated as idempotent, unguarded None returns, full GET/PUT to flip one flag, unverified trigger/delivery conditions, unknown network reachability, auth-method invariants. Mocks mirror the assumption, so it fails only against the real service.
trigger_signals: a new client method for a third-party list/create/update endpoint
a webhook/bot integration with delivery or trigger conditions, or a push to a service whose host is unstated
provisioning accounts or changing auth methods in an external system
uploading a large binary (AAB/IPA over ~50MB) through googleapiclient/httplib2

a poll/settle parser or error reader written from a vendor integration guide; a webhook-only payment rail (bank wire, virtual IBAN) handled with the redirect rail's correlation key; synthetic identifiers generated for a provider field
a Play Publisher edits.commit or App Store Connect reviewSubmissions call scripted for the first time, or for an app's first-ever submission
an integration needs two same-vendor credential types (GitHub OAuth App vs GitHub App); pinning an input on a third-party CI action to remove its network call

a cluster bootstrapped with a placeholder pull secret, followed by an in-cluster build (BuildConfig / oc start-build), dynamic PVC provisioning, or any platform pod restart after a DiskPressure image GC
relying on Spark/Athena/Glue/AWS SDK behavior (lazy evaluation, recursiveFileLookup, static confs, crawler lag, SDK omitting empty arrays, Athena writer caps)
preventive_checks: Read the provider docs for pagination, empty bodies, error ids, partial-update endpoints and trigger conditions, and write them down
Contract-test with recorded real responses: 204/empty body, page 2, the specific error body, None
Confirm network direction and reachability before choosing push vs dial-out
Use a chunked resumable MediaFileUpload with a timeout of at least 600s and http.follow_redirects = False, and test with a real full-size artifact

Hit the live/sandbox endpoint once and assert the real payload shape and error-key casing; write the webhook test from a notification payload that carries no internal payment id; generate synthetic ids to the provider's documented format and test that format

Submit an app's first-ever version through the store console (it names the real blocking field); retry a Play commit once with changesNotSentForReview toggled on the 400 naming it, and log which branch ran

Name each credential type by exact product, settings URL and the capability it serves before asking the user; read the action's action.yml/entrypoint to confirm which code path an input actually skips

On a placeholder-secret cluster treat every platform feature whose images come from the authenticated registry as untested: check builder/CSI image registries first, plan an external build (podman) and static/hostPath volumes up front, and after any DiskPressure or eviction event confirm CSI, registry and ingress pods are Running before relying on them
Check engine/SDK docs for the exact behavior and test the edge (empty arrays, lazy action after cleanup, same-day partitions) once

FS-44.name: Migration unsafe for code or data already in the shared DB
FS-44.mechanism: A migration is right for the new code but not for what already exists: NOT NULL columns without db_default applied to a DB shared with older deployed code or parallel agents, constraints older code violates, role/RLS DDL needing privileges the app user lacks, raw SQL without cross-app dependencies, behavior flips with no backfill for existing rows.
trigger_signals: a new NOT NULL column or DB constraint on a table staging and prod share
a migration with raw SQL on another app's table, or role/privilege DDL
a feature flips an enablement flow for rows created under the old flow
staging and prod share one DB and the change alters the shape of rows (nesting, new parent links) that the deployed prod code also reads or writes
preventive_checks: Set db_default (or nullable + backfill) for new required fields; run sqlmigrate and reject bare ADD COLUMN NOT NULL on shared tables
Confirm every currently deployed code path honors a new constraint before it reaches the shared DB
Check rolsuper/CREATEROLE of the target DB role, and declare explicit cross-app migration dependencies
Ship a backfill with any behavior change and test it on pre-existing rows
Make the deployed code tolerate the new row shape first, or schedule the prod deploy right after staging; test the old code path against new-shape rows

FS-45.name: Agent turn ends waiting on an unverified async mechanism
FS-45.mechanism: A (sub)agent hands its completion to something asynchronous it never verified (its own Monitor watcher, a wakeup timer, a blocking debug call, a resumed run) and ends idle, wedged or silent with uncommitted edits. The orchestrator then waits or assumes failure instead of checking git and test state directly. Release automation adds background pollers that shell out to helpers in /tmp which vanish between sessions and then fail silently every cycle, background uploads and scratch dirs from a previous session with no completion record, a background subagent that crashed at launch, and a laptop that sleeps mid-pipeline. Fan-out lifecycle gaps compound it: more agents than the runtime's concurrency cap, stopped parents whose nested helpers keep running, and consumers launched when the producer's file appears rather than when it finishes.
trigger_signals: a worker's last action is starting a background run/Monitor and waiting for its notification
a blocking call against a live server or browser that can hang
a subagent silent for an unusually long time, or a promise of periodic updates on a timer
a subagent backgrounds its own long command and yields; multi-hour fan-out state held only in process; a fix loop planned around resuming agents via SendMessage
a background poll/loop shells out to a helper under /tmp or a scratch dir; resuming after hours or a session boundary on a background task's result; a long unattended release run on a laptop
dispatching three or more long-running worktree agents at once
an implementer has run many consecutive fix rounds in one session without committing (provider session/rate limits end it mid-round)
background implementer agents running when the parent session may hit a usage limit; planning to resume a subagent via SendMessage
dispatching more than ~20 background agents in one go (the runtime's concurrent-subagent cap)
stopping a parent agent whose brief lets it dispatch nested helpers
a producer agent still running while its output file already exists on disk, or several producers writing into one inbox that a later step globs
a bench, Playwright batch or suite whose last wall exceeded ~5 min run in the foreground: the Bash tool's 600 s limit silently moves it to the background
a next step planned as 'sleep N then read the log' (the harness blocks foreground sleep polling)
preventive_checks: Instruct workers to run verification synchronously or poll results themselves, never ending a turn on their own watcher
Background potentially hanging calls and poll with a timeout
When a subagent stalls, check git status/log and test results directly before relaunching
Put 'never background a command, run to completion' in every agent prompt template, checkpoint fan-out progress to a durable file, and confirm the resume tool is available before planning around it

Keep automation helpers in the repo's scripts/, make poll loops exit non-zero when a helper is missing, check a dispatched agent's output file size/mtime shortly after launch, treat a missing completion record as unknown and re-verify against the target system (ASC/Play), and run caffeinate for long unattended runs
Arm a per-worktree file-write staleness watch and check the session/rate budget before the fan-out
Commit after each discrete fix and write self-contained round briefs so a fresh agent can resume a round if the previous one dies
After any session restart check each in-flight worktree's git status before assuming work landed; hand off through a persisted report file a fresh agent reads, since SendMessage may be disabled
Check the runtime's concurrent-subagent cap and dispatch in batches under it
When cancelling a parent, list and stop its descendants too, then confirm nothing is still running
Dispatch consumers only on the producer's completion notification, never on file existence; aggregation reads a closed per-producer manifest instead of globbing a shared inbox
Size each foreground run under ~8 min, or launch with run_in_background plus a Monitor until-loop on the summary line; never end the turn before the summary and exit code exist
Integrators reject any lane report whose benchmark or suite result lacks the exit code and numbers

FS-51.name: Code handles one of several representations of the same fact
FS-51.mechanism: The same real-world fact is stored or transmitted several ways: a bank match as an FK or a batch M2M, account_type as a slug or a title-cased label, names with case/slug variants, location scope as a query param or a header, a file on the parent M2M or on per-section child fields, an orphan as a null FK or a detached non-null FK, URL scope under several param names. A query, merge key, guard, finder or test is written against the one representation the author saw first and declared exhaustive, so rows in the other representation slip through.
trigger_signals: a guard, finder or 'is matched/reconciled' check follows one relation path between two models
a grouping/merge key uses a raw type or name field that other code canonicalizes
request scope can arrive via query param or header; a guard allow-lists known URL param names
a cleanup is verified by searching for the exact string or anomaly signature named in the ticket
a cross-cutting feature (file tracking, audit) wired to the first model found carrying the field
a stored-file URL field can hold several URI schemes (s3://, gs://, https) and presigning is wired for only one; the field is rendered as an href in more than one component
an exclude/ignore list names one build-output dir (.next) in a repo that also holds suffixed variants (.next-live, .next-e2e, .next-verify)
comparing file paths that come from different producers (absolute vs repo-relative, ./ prefixes)
preventive_checks: Grep the schema for every FK/M2M/through relation linking the two models and every model carrying the field type; cover and test each path
SELECT DISTINCT the stored values of every key component org-wide before writing a merge key, and reuse the canonicalization the bucket router already uses
Resolve scope through the existing helper that honors every input channel (scope_to_locations / effective_location_ids) and test the header-only entry point
Verify cleanups with a broader case-insensitive/pattern search and check the sibling signature (null FK vs detached FK) before declaring done
Enumerate every link builder that targets a guarded route and test each param variant
Contract-test that every URL field in API responses starts with https:// for each configured storage backend, and grep every component that renders the field
Exclude by glob (.next*), then du -sh the staged context and compare it with the source size before shipping
Normalize both sides to resolved repo-relative paths before comparing, and test absolute, ./-prefixed and relative inputs

FS-53.name: Known fix or learned rule not made durable, so the same trap recurs
FS-53.mechanism: A root cause is found and fixed on a branch, filed as a chip, or taught by the user, but never carried to where it stops recurring: the fix sits unpromoted at some hop of the promotion chain (or pushed with no PR), the filed durable fix is never implemented, a pending migration is never landed, a faster tool or new safety rule never reaches the skill's default recipe or the scripts already written. The symptom keeps firing in production and is hand-healed, costing a round each time.
trigger_signals: the same symptom class shows up a second time, or a manual cleanup/sweep is being run again
a fix was 'pushed' but no promotion PR is open, or it has not reached main
a chip/TODO for the durable fix already exists for the error you are re-patching
the user states a rule correcting a mistake, or a new tool supersedes the documented recipe
every branch has to detect-and-ignore the same drift (unmade migration, scanner false positive)
a release helper or upload fix being recreated ad hoc for the second time; a session ending with a diagnosed fix deliberately held back
the same failure is flagged 'pre-existing, not my change' in two or more sessions
a process gap hit once in a parallel batch while other tickets in the same batch are still queued
preventive_checks: On the second occurrence treat the root-cause fix as blocking: report its branch -> PR -> promotion stage and count only 'merged to main and deployed' as done
Keep one visible list mapping recurring bug classes to fix branches and their promotion stage, and surface it every time the class fires
Write a user-taught rule or a new default tool into the skill/runbook immediately, then grep previously written fix scripts for violations
Land shared drift fixes (pending migration, scanner excludes, allowlists) once on main instead of working around them per branch
Commit hardened helpers into scripts/ on the first fix; write a held-back diagnosis and its next action to a ticket or memory before the session ends
Once a failure is confirmed pre-existing twice, fix it or file and link a ticket instead of re-flagging it
Add the learned step to every remaining brief and reviewer checklist in the batch immediately

FS-55.name: Rule keyed on a proxy signal instead of the defining type, status or link
FS-55.mechanism: A posting rule, detector, cleanup or guard decides membership from something that usually correlates with the real condition: notes text ('TR FR/TO ...'), the existence of a downstream leg instead of the counterpart FK, an is_matched flag that ORs manual reconciliation with structural pairing, a denormalized date copy instead of the linked rows, a structural flag instead of account_type, every row in a source list without checking department_type, every status instead of the ones the balance sheet reads. Inputs where proxy and truth diverge are silently mis-posted, mis-flagged or deleted.
trigger_signals: a filter matches free text, notes or naming conventions to identify a class of financial row
a 'matched/unmatched' or 'safe to delete' decision inferred from a side effect or a conflated boolean
a business rule says 'only bank-type accounts' / 'only merchandise rows' / 'only REVIEWED' and the function never references that field
a lock or invariant check reads a denormalized copy on the mutated model
a build/config guard greps a whole file for a placeholder string instead of reading the one key it validates; a test-data cleanup selects rows by guessing their generated naming pattern
a cache-hit or fast-path early return tests only the fields one writer fills (transcript present) while the response promises more fields (summary, scores) that another path derives
classifying tests or endpoints as read-only by HTTP verb or URL while GET handlers may lazily get_or_create shared rows
preventive_checks: Filter on the defining field (account_type, department_type, status, the counterpart FK resolved in both directions) and add a fixture with the same text/shape but a different type/status that must be excluded
Split conflated booleans into separately named signals and have each consumer query the one it means
Enumerate every status/lifecycle value of the source model and state which ones the rule covers
Key cleanups and lookups on the canonical identity the sync writer uses ((source_type, source_id)) and resolve the real linked rows, not copies
Read the exact key path (plutil/jq) in config guards and test with a filled value plus a stale comment; mark test rows at creation and clean up by exact match, not by regex
Make the early-return condition list every field the response promises, and test with only the webhook-written fields populated
Back static read-only claims with a row-level DB write audit and flag get_or_create in GET handlers

FS-61.name: Credentials echoed into output or passed as plaintext config
FS-61.mechanism: Settings/startup code prints credentials fetched from the secret manager, and a shared ops box's login-shell profile echoes the prod DB credential as a banner. Any SSM, CI or agent command run through manage.py shell or a login shell (bash -lc, sudo -i, ssh with a profile) captures the secret into logs and transcripts. The trap is known and noted in memory but not fixed, so it recurs on every remote-ops task.
trigger_signals: about to run a command on a remote box via a login shell, sudo -i, or manage.py shell
settings/startup code logs or prints resolved secrets
memory notes a credential-echo trap on a box you are about to use
a Secrets Manager ARN or Pulumi requireSecret value flowing into a container environment map
preventive_checks: Invoke remote commands with a non-login shell (bash --noprofile --norc, no -l/-i) and prefer management commands or script files over manage.py shell
Grep settings/startup code and the box's shell profile for print/log/echo of secret values and remove them at the source; rotate any credential that appeared in output
Track the leak as a blocking ops item, not a memory note, and scrub secret-shaped strings from output before surfacing it
Pass secrets via ECS/Batch secrets valueFrom, never as plain env values

FS-62.name: Bug class fixed in one template-copied sibling survives in the others
FS-62.mechanism: A family of near-identical functions for different entity types (one ledger-posting function per source type such as deposit, expense, merchandise and fuel; a P&L report module beside a balance-sheet report module; backfill scripts beside the pipeline) was built by copying one template. A bug in the template (child-row date/location/organization instead of the parent daily entry's, update_or_create keyed on one FK, a NULL-excluding filter, abs() after aggregate, a status gate for one subtype) is fixed where it was reported, and the other copies keep it until each is rediscovered in a later reconciliation round.
trigger_signals: fixing a bug in one function whose name follows a family pattern (a shared posting-function prefix, *_view, fix_*)
the fix changes how a field is sourced (date, location, organization) or how a lookup is keyed
a gate or rule exists for one subtype (expense checks) of a model with sibling subtypes
preventive_checks: After the fix, grep every sibling in the family (and adjacent backfill/fix scripts) for the same pattern and fix or document each before calling it done
Diff sibling functions line by line for field sourcing and lookup keys, and enumerate every field copied from the wrong source, not just the one that triggered the bug
Add one regression test per sibling or subtype, and extract the shared piece into a helper

FS-63.name: Entity identity matched on a non-identifying attribute
FS-63.mechanism: Scripts, importers and pickers decide which real-world entity a row refers to by a display name, .first() of several candidates, or a (payee, amount, date) coincidence, while the data has names repeated across orgs/locations, several bank accounts per location, dangling duplicates from delete-then-recreate, and legitimate same-amount instruments. The opposite error also occurs: exact FK equality treats punctuation-variant duplicate payees as different entities. The wrong row gets linked, voided, skipped or created.
trigger_signals: resolving a location, account or bank account by name or .first() in a multi-org / multi-account setting
treating rows as duplicates because payee/amount/date match
a match predicate in a reconciliation script that lacks the identity field (employee name, check number)
guarding on FK equality in a domain with known near-duplicate master records
a data migration dedups or groups by a business key without the tenant/repository id
a reconcile/reindex step that runs per page or partition while row identity is unique per document; match keys that are mutable attributes or list positions
output files or ids keyed on a value that repeats across sources (session id in two dirs) or derived from enumeration order while another artifact persists references to them
preventive_checks: Resolve by a unique key (id, check/invoice number) scoped by organization and location; when the input lacks one, require the column or flag every ambiguous row instead of taking .first()
Query all candidates sharing the name across orgs and confirm against a reference point the user gave before creating or mutating
Spot-check a known-unique row to confirm the match predicate discriminates; filter to currently linked rows (e.g. daily_entries__isnull=False) in models with dangling duplicates
Ask before treating a same-amount/same-date record as a duplicate
Include the tenant key in dedup group-bys and test the same canonical id present in two tenants in different states
Match on the stable id at the identity's full uniqueness scope (document, not page); test moving content across partitions, editing matched attributes, and inserting/renumbering items
Persist ids once into the source records and key outputs on (source, id)

FS-65.name: Which host, checkout or branch serves an environment assumed
FS-65.mechanism: Boxes keep a manual git checkout beside the CodeDeploy-served directory, services track a branch other than the one just pushed, a staging hostname hits the dev backend while sharing the prod DB, and only one box ships logs to the central store. Verification, restarts, migration checks and forensics run against whichever host or directory is at hand and produce clean-looking but wrong answers ('deployed', 'no logs', 'migrated').
trigger_signals: verifying deployed code or migration state on a box, or advising 'restart to pick up the change'
searching a central log store for a non-prod hostname's traffic
installing a long-running service against an ad hoc checkout while the pipeline is blocked
about to conclude that evidence or logs are unrecoverable
a prod manage.py run after sourcing .env.prod without --settings or an exported DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE
preventive_checks: Read the service's systemd unit WorkingDirectory and venv, then check git -C <that dir> rev-parse HEAD and its branch before verifying or restarting
Confirm which backend host serves each hostname and whether its logs ship before searching; enumerate known hosts (deploy config, DNS, known_hosts) before declaring data unrecoverable
Track any service pointed at a manual checkout as temporary and re-point it at the deploy target before calling the rollout done
Pass --settings explicitly and print the resolved settings module and DB host as the first output line of any prod ops command

FS-66.name: Session-scoped cloud or CLI credentials assumed still valid
FS-66.mechanism: AWS SSO tokens and CLI OAuth logins expire within hours, and long sessions, sub-sessions and bench runs inherit the same expired state. Investigations, downloads and tunnels start without an identity check and fail mid-flight, sometimes after partial work, and the same expiry recurs after each multi-hour gap.
trigger_signals: starting remote diagnostics, an SSM/tunnel session, a cloud download or a local bench run
a multi-hour gap since the last cloud command in the session
spawning a sub-session that inherits local CLI auth
an admin task starts with gcloud compute ssh or other gcloud calls under an org policy that forces periodic interactive reauth
a gcloud scp/ssh production write late in a long session
a merged PR's deploy step queued hours after the gcloud login in the same agent session
an exported AWS_PROFILE from an earlier command in a persistent shell, a prod profile in a non-default credentials file, a stale CodeArtifact token, or pulumi config get ... 2>/dev/null
preventive_checks: Run a cheap identity check first (aws sts get-caller-identity, CLI auth status) and ask the user to re-auth up front if it fails
Re-check at the start of every task that opens a new tunnel/SSM session, and short-circuit dependent runs on the first auth failure instead of retrying each blind
Keep a documented fallback path (SSH key) for remote access
Check gcloud auth validity first and surface reauth immediately; prefer a service-account identity for headless admin scripts
Run gcloud auth print-access-token before staging files and again right before the write
Run gcloud auth print-access-token right before any queued deploy step and use a deploy-scoped service account instead of a personal OAuth session for automated deploys

Print aws sts get-caller-identity before each account-specific command, list profiles from both config and credentials files, scope AWS_PROFILE per command, refresh CodeArtifact tokens before install, and never silence stderr of secret fetches

FS-84.name: Dependency or toolchain change not resolved against what actually installs and runs
FS-84.mechanism: A package bump, override, version pin or tool-command migration is written as intent and never checked against the resolved result: a `>=` override lets pnpm jump a major version past the consumer's range, the pnpm that corepack resolves needs a newer Node than .nvmrc pins, a bump of the Playwright test package needs its matching browser binaries, and replacing `next lint` with `eslint .` silently widens the linted tree. The lockfile and the first run look fine until a fresh host, a fresh environment or a second verification pass hits it.
trigger_signals: adding a pnpm/npm override or resolution for a security patch
bumping the Playwright test package, Next, ESLint or another tool whose runtime assets or config format are coupled to its version
provisioning a host where Node/corepack is installed separately from the repo's .nvmrc and packageManager field
replacing a framework-scoped command (next lint) with a bare tool invocation (eslint .)
removing a package from requirements to escape a native-extension crash (cryptography SIGILL on an arm64 VM) while another installed package still imports it transitively (pymysql _auth)
preventive_checks: Write overrides as a caret range within the patched major (^4.3.2) and confirm the resolved version with pnpm why or the lockfile before committing
Pin packageManager explicitly and check that .nvmrc's Node satisfies the engines of the package manager and tools before provisioning
Make `playwright install` for the pinned version part of the bump commit's steps and of every fresh environment's pre-e2e setup; print tool versions before trusting lint/typecheck output
When migrating lint or type commands, re-create the old scope with explicit ignores and diff the error count against the pre-migration baseline
After removing a dependency, pip show / pip list inside the built image to confirm it is gone and run a bare import smoke test in a throwaway container on the target arch

FS-90.name: Repo tooling bound to one machine's interpreter or to an unprovisioned worktree
FS-90.mechanism: Git hooks and test entry points hardcode an absolute interpreter path (a python.org framework build) or assume `python` is on PATH, and new worktrees ship without a venv. On another machine or worktree the hook can't start, or runs an interpreter that lacks native wheels and blocks by design. Each session then rediscovers which Python has pytest and the parsers, installs them by hand, and pushes with --no-verify.
trigger_signals: a committed git hook or script references an absolute interpreter path (/Library/Frameworks/Python.framework/..., /opt/homebrew/bin/python3.x)
the first git push from this machine or worktree in the session
starting work in a fresh agent worktree checkout with no .venv and no `python` on PATH, on a host with several system Pythons
the hook needs native extension wheels (tree_sitter parsers) that only one installed interpreter has
e2e/backend scripts or spec helpers that resolve Python as <checkout>/.venv/bin/python run from a worktree with no venv
committing, pushing or linting from a fresh agent-managed or /tmp worktree of a Yarn monorepo (no node_modules; husky/lint-staged hooks need yarn)
preventive_checks: Make hooks resolve the interpreter in order (repo .venv, then PATH python3) and check required imports up front with a clear message instead of a silent block
Ship one bootstrap command (make venv / scripts/setup) that builds the pinned-version venv with requirements plus test deps, and run it as step 0 in every new worktree
Before any documented --no-verify escape, run the exact gate the hook would run with the working venv and paste its green result into the PR body
After the second bypass, fix the hook on main instead of bypassing it again (FS-53)
Route every helper's interpreter through one resolver honoring an interpreter-override env variable, and create or link the venv as part of worktree creation

Run yarn install (and the job's poetry install) as step 0 in every new worktree before tests, lint or commit; use the repo-documented runner (the job's test-runner script, the documented ts-node invocation and compiler options)

FS-91.name: Written claim in docs, comments or commit prose not re-derived from what it cites
FS-91.mechanism: Docstrings, whitepaper paragraphs, case source fields, adjudications and commit bodies state facts from the plan's prediction, from memory or from a copied note, not from a fresh run or a read of the source. Examples: 'this case now passes', 'this case proves end-to-end routing', a precedent's numbers, another file's note on wiring status. Reviewers catch the mismatch late, or it misdirects later planning.
trigger_signals: writing a docstring, comment or doc sentence saying a named test or case passes or proves a behavior
quoting another file's descriptive note (catalog notes, scope or wiring status) into new docs or a case's source field
a commit body, adjudication or PR description citing numbers, thresholds or commit history from another document
prose written in the same session as the plan that predicted the outcome
a hand-assembled .patch file or apply instruction committed into a report
preventive_checks: Run the exact test or case and cite its result next to any 'now passes' claim; if it still fails, write the outcome as expected, not achieved
Before describing what a case proves, trace the runner function it actually invokes and name that code path
Re-verify any quoted state note against current code instead of copying it
Open the cited document and quote its exact numbers and SHAs instead of paraphrasing from memory
Produce patch notes with git diff from a scratch branch and run git apply --check on a clean checkout before committing

FS-99.name: Document-parsing heuristic tuned on synthetic or single sample documents
FS-99.mechanism: Parsers and change detectors for real-world documents (Word BRDs through pandoc, meeting transcripts, minutes) are built against synthetic fixtures or tuned from one real sample: a colon-prefix speaker rule, a TOC line pattern, a heading-level rule, a noise-suppression skip rule. The next document differs (heading style != numbering, TOC kept as content, requirements authored as tables, a body that is all front matter, 'Action items:' headings), and the heuristic misreads or deletes real content. The real-document gate runs last, so the misfit surfaces at the end of the build.
trigger_signals: a spec names real-document risk for an import/parse feature while all fixtures are synthetic
changing a parsing heuristic because of one real document
a skip or strip rule keyed on a loose line pattern or an absence condition (no anchors, colon prefix, TOC-shaped line)
regex/denylist/fallback rules over scraped bios, URLs or vendor payloads built from a few bad examples or self-authored fixtures
preventive_checks: Get several real documents at plan time (ask the user for customer samples) and run the real-document import gate from the first parser task, not in a final lane

Keep a corpus of edge-shaped fixtures (style != numbering, TOC, table-authored requirements, doc-control tables, an all-front-matter body, 'Heading:' lines) and run every heuristic change against all of them

Give every removal or skip heuristic a negative example, confirm matches against structure (TOC entries map to real headings) before deleting content, and guard a generalized fix with the condition of the sample it came from
Run the rule over a real prod sample and inspect both what it rejects and positive examples it must keep

FS-109.name: Waiting state with no deadline when its resolver disappears
FS-109.mechanism: A record or process enters a waiting state (pending, updating, held, mismatch) whose only exit is an event from another actor: a watcher, a callback, a renderer or a follow-up flow. When that actor dies, restarts or is never started, nothing moves the state on and it holds forever: a node stops sending heartbeats, a run never settles, a badge says updating indefinitely. Tests always drive the resolver, so the never-resolves path is first exercised live.
trigger_signals: a new pending, held or verifying state that is cleared only by another process, callback or user action
a hold that suppresses a liveness signal (heartbeat, lease renewal) until a check passes
a watcher or supervisor process that may be absent after a restart or an upgrade
preventive_checks: For every waiting state write down the event that ends it and a deadline that moves it to a reported terminal state (failed, rolled back)
Test the resolver never arriving: kill the watcher or drop the callback, advance the clock past the deadline, and assert the state ends and liveness resumes

L-data-shape-assumed-not-read.name: Data type, unit, layout or source assumed from a name or sample instead of read from the producer
L-data-shape-assumed-not-read.mechanism: Queries, schemas, joins and DQ checks are written from a column's name, a pasted sample, a test fixture, a TS interface or a couple of sampled files: string dates treated as DATE, epoch unit guessed, partition layout asserted, a Glue/Spark schema typed from field names, a similar column taken from the wrong table, uniqueness or absence-as-NULL assumed. Code runs and returns plausible numbers, so the mismatch shows only when a user checks real rows.
trigger_signals: writing SQL/PySpark against a table or column not yet inspected in this session
a type, unit or format inferred from a field name (user_id, created_at, *_code) or a single pasted value
hand-writing a Glue/StructType/DDL schema for a vendor payload or from a design doc
two tables expose a similarly named column, or a dedup is removed because a table is 'already unique'
a backfill over months of files whose encoding was checked on one or two samples
claims about what an API returns derived from type definitions or mapper code
preventive_checks: Read the producer first: Glue schema (get-table), the writer's partition_keys/MERGE key, or the mapper that emits the field
Sample real rows (DISTINCT, min/max, typeof, count by format) across the full date range before fixing a type, unit, grain or encoding boundary
Check join-key uniqueness with GROUP BY key HAVING count(*)>1 before joining or dropping a dedup
Validate a hand-written schema against one real payload/parquet file per time slice
State the source table and column for every metric before computing it

L-unrequested-scope-or-deviation.name: Change exceeds or deviates from the explicit ask
L-unrequested-scope-or-deviation.mechanism: The agent adds things nobody asked for (feature flags, bypasses, filters, extra alarms, speculative parsing, one-off abstractions, refactors, version bumps, prod-mutating migrations), substitutes its own design, method or evidence source for the one named, or silently changes a derivation or invariant while doing a narrow edit. Reviewers must then unpick unrelated diff and the requested behavior is subtly different.
trigger_signals: the request is a short imperative (remove X, rename Y, add Z to these N places)
the user names a target function, method of verification, table set or rule
copying a sibling pattern that carries a flag, guard or abstraction the ask didn't mention
the diff is much larger than the ask, or touches a shared helper/lib for a single-service ask
a delegation prompt paraphrases the user's rules for a subagent
preventive_checks: Before finishing, walk every hunk and map it to a sentence in the ask; revert hunks that map to nothing or call them out as questions
Use the exact function, evidence source and tables the user named; ask before substituting
Never add exceptions to an access/deny rule, relax an assert into a fallback, or delete a feature to resolve a bug without asking
Pass the user's requirement verbatim to subagents instead of paraphrasing it
Keep temporary instrumentation minimal and local; no structural rewrites

L-runtime-or-dialect-mismatch.name: Code targets a runtime, engine version or SQL dialect other than the one that executes it
L-runtime-or-dialect-mismatch.mechanism: Code is written for the local or most familiar runtime: Python 3.10+ syntax/stdlib on EMR's Python 3.9, implicit namespace packages under zipimport, Spark SQL DDL/MERGE given to Athena/Trino, JVM Spark API names in PySpark, regex/escaping/case/integer semantics that differ across engines, newer library or provider kwargs than the pinned version. Local tests pass on the newer runtime; the failure appears only on the cluster or engine.
trigger_signals: editing batch-job source or a spark-submit entrypoint that ships to EMR
writing SQL without stating the engine (Athena/Trino vs Spark vs Postgres vs sharded Postgres)
porting a regex, hash compare, cast or arithmetic expression from one engine/language to another
using an API/kwarg found in current docs while the repo pins an older library/provider version
a new PySpark package dir or src.zip --py-files packaging
preventive_checks: Name the executing runtime and version before writing code; for EMR keep 3.9-compatible (no X|Y, match, StrEnum, importlib.resources.files)
Check the target engine's docs for each DDL/DML/function (Athena ALTER TABLE, Trino CTE inlining, to_hex case, JSON cast) or run it once there
Check the pinned version in pyproject/lock before using a newer API, kwarg or function
Add __init__.py to every package dir that ships in a zip, and import-test the zip with python3.9
Run one representative query/job on the real engine before handing it over

L-query-plan-cost-at-scale.name: Query or Spark job shape whose cost explodes at production scale
L-query-plan-cost-at-scale.mechanism: The job is correct on a sample but its plan does not scale: repeated count()/collect() actions on uncached lineage, array_contains or fuzzy predicates forcing nested-loop joins, filters on non-partition columns, partition specs that ignore the dominant join key, whole-table MERGE/scan for per-batch work, shard-key-less queries on sharded Postgres, aggregate-then-LIMIT pagination, predicate pushdown re-inlining expensive expressions.
trigger_signals: a transform calls count()/first()/collect() for logging or emptiness checks
a join condition is a function over an array or a non-equi/fuzzy predicate
a new Iceberg table DDL or a query filter on a large staging/curated table
a MERGE or dedup that scans the full history for a small batch
ad-hoc plain or sharded Postgres query without the shard key; DISTINCT ON/GROUP BY before LIMIT
preventive_checks: Run explain() / EXPLAIN on the real table and check join strategy, partition pruning and shard fan-out
Read the table's partition spec before claiming a filter prunes; choose partitions from the dominant downstream access path
Compute several metrics in one cached aggregation; use isEmpty/limit(1) instead of count()
Bound dedup/MERGE to the current batch keys and partitions
Paginate before aggregating; include the shard key in sharded-database predicates

L-capacity-without-platform-math.name: Capacity, concurrency or quota set without the platform's resource math
L-capacity-without-platform-math.mechanism: Memory, vCPU, executor counts, thread pools, parallel transfers and task counts are tuned from a hypothesis or copied numbers without checking the platform's fixed limits (EMR Serverless memory/vCPU ratios, Batch CE overhead, account quotas), the host's size, per-host S3 limits, connection-pool sizes or shared quotas like a vendor thread pool. Jobs OOM, get throttled, or exceed a quota that the test account still had room for.
trigger_signals: changing cpu/memory/executor/initialCapacity settings for EMR Serverless, EMR or Batch
copying parallelism defaults from a bigger machine or a daily job to a backfill
a thread pool around a boto3 client, or scaling tasks that share a capped external pool
adding a quota-capped AWS resource (on-demand Kinesis stream, Batch CE) in prod
preventive_checks: Read the Pulumi worker size and the service's documented limits before editing Spark conf; fit conf to infra, not infra to guesses
Compute concurrency x per-unit memory against the instance; leave agent/OS overhead on Batch
Match boto3 max_pool_connections to thread count; model shared quotas (vendor thread pools) from measured peak, not stated baseline
Check current account quota usage in prod before adding capped resources
Size backfill windows from per-run shuffle volume, not calendar units

L-git-action-on-unchecked-branch.name: Git commit, reset or push run without checking the current branch and PR state
L-git-action-on-unchecked-branch.mechanism: The agent commits, resets or pushes on whatever is checked out: directly on the base branch, on an unrelated feature branch, on a branch whose PR already squash-merged (recreating it), in a worktree on the wrong branch, or after switching back to base and writing follow-ups there. Partial commits leave imports to uncommitted files, and deleted worktrees keep holding branches.
trigger_signals: about to commit/push via a UI action or a one-line command
returning to a PR branch after hours or days
the current branch name doesn't relate to the change, or is the base branch (dev/main)
creating or removing a worktree; staging only some of the changed files
preventive_checks: Run git status -sb and gh pr view --json state,headRefName before every commit/push
Never commit to the base branch; create a branch with --no-track from origin/<base>
If the PR is merged, start a new branch from origin/<base>
Check staged files import nothing unstaged (git stash -k && build) before a partial commit
Remove worktrees with git worktree remove, then git worktree prune

L-orchestrator-schedule-semantics.name: Orchestrator schedule, catchup, timeout or trigger semantics changed without re-deriving dependents
L-orchestrator-schedule-semantics.mechanism: Airflow DAG cadence, catchup, start_date, execution_timeout, waiter attempts, trigger rules, TaskGroup factories and XCom flows are edited in isolation: lookback and day-of-month logic still assume the old cadence, catchup replays from a stale start_date, timeouts are shorter than the external job and retries start a second writer, fixed task_ids collide in factories, wall-clock values are recomputed across an approval gate, and recovery advice relies on XCom from a hand-marked task.
trigger_signals: changing schedule_interval/cron, catchup or start_date
adding an EMR/Batch operator or sensor with waiter_max_attempts or execution_timeout
a fan-in task after .expand(), or a TaskGroup factory called per platform
tasks that each compute dates from now(), or a recovery plan that marks tasks success
preventive_checks: Grep the DAG for every value derived from the schedule (lookback, day-of-month, data_interval) and update them together
Size timeouts and waiter attempts x delay to the measured p99 job runtime; confirm retries terminate the underlying job
When enabling catchup, move start_date to the deploy date
Compute time-derived values once and pass them via XCom/params; ensure downstream tasks tolerate a hand-marked upstream

L-iam-guessed-not-enumerated.name: IAM policy written from SDK names or memory instead of the client's actual API calls
L-iam-guessed-not-enumerated.mechanism: Policies are drafted from SDK method names, guessed condition attribute names, or 'least privilege' intuition: tools like rsync need list/read on the destination, ListBucket is evaluated on the bucket resource with s3:prefix including parent prefixes, condition keys apply only to some actions, managed services read with their own service agent, new principals need propagation time. A missing grant gets 'fixed' with a wildcard.
trigger_signals: writing a least-privilege policy for a CLI/tool or managed service
an action name copied from an SDK method (HeadObject, ListObjectsV2)
a prefix-scoped condition or a CEL/condition key typed from memory
AccessDenied on one resource in an allow-list policy
preventive_checks: Look up each action and condition key in the service authorization reference
Enumerate the API calls the tool makes (CloudTrail, --debug) and grant exactly those
Add the missing resource rather than a wildcard; include parent prefixes in s3:prefix conditions
Grant managed-service agents explicitly and wait for/verify principal propagation

L-cloud-resource-config-unvalidated.name: Cloud resource args or capability assumed without checking the provider schema and service rules
L-cloud-resource-config-unvalidated.mechanism: New resource types and configs are written from console concepts or docs for a different context: SEARCH metric math in alarms (dashboard-only), incompatible crawler policies, SELECT * in BCM exports, global services on the regional provider, CFN types not in the region, datapoints-to-alarm exceeding evaluation periods, updates rejected while an app is STARTED, control-plane rate limits under Pulumi parallelism. Preview passes; deploy fails.
trigger_signals: first use of a Pulumi resource type in the repo
an alarm/metric-math expression, a crawler/export config, or a global-region service
updating an EMR Serverless application or other resource with state-dependent update rules
a dynamic provider creating many resources of one type
preventive_checks: Read the Pulumi/Terraform provider schema and the AWS API constraints for every arg before writing
Check region availability for new resource types (cloudformation describe-type) and use a us-east-1 provider for global services
Validate alarm math and periods against CloudWatch alarm restrictions
Deploy once to a personal stack before merging a first-of-kind resource

L-refactor-drops-behavior.name: Refactor or rewrite silently drops behavior the original had
L-refactor-drops-behavior.mechanism: Extracting into a shared helper, consolidating files, renaming, or rewriting a body by hand rather than moving it loses steps (warm-up, classloader semantics, existence checks, dependency order, fields, docstrings) or smuggles logic changes into a 'mechanical' change. Nothing fails until the dropped behavior is needed.
trigger_signals: extracting working code into a shared library or factory
merging several files, or a 'rename only' task that also touches bodies
rewriting a class/function body that has docstrings, guards or ordering
preventive_checks: Move code verbatim first, then diff old vs new and account for every removed line
Keep rename-only commits free of body edits
Diff task dependency order before and after a TaskGroup/factory extraction
Run the original call path's tests against the refactored code

L-copied-sibling-unaudited.name: Sibling module copied wholesale without auditing what it carries
L-copied-sibling-unaudited.mechanism: A new lambda, infra file, bucket, DQ suite or table is cloned from a sibling and keeps its baggage: unrenamed identifiers, import-time env reads for unset vars, IAM and env vars the new use never needs, legacy versioning state, deprecated patterns, layer placement and thresholds that fit the sibling only.
trigger_signals: creating a file by copying a sibling module or 'exactly the same' resource
a sibling resource with historical or legacy config
per-platform suites or configs generated from one template
preventive_checks: After copying, grep for the sibling's name and walk each env var, grant and setting asking whether the new one reads it
Check provider deprecations before copying a pattern
Derive thresholds/config per target from its own data, not the sibling's values

L-downstream-patch-instead-of-producer.name: Consumer or edge patched to tolerate bad state instead of fixing the producer
L-downstream-patch-instead-of-producer.mechanism: When one producer emits inconsistent state, the fix lands in a shared consumer (per-table flag in a shared job, override in the optimizer), at the outermost presentation mapper, in the data to satisfy a validator, or as a hardcoded field list. Other consumers still see the bad state and shared code grows special cases.
trigger_signals: a review says a shared job breaks on one new table/producer
the quickest fix is a flag or field list in shared/downstream code
a bug visible in one API surface that re-maps an upstream service
preventive_checks: Trace the bad value to the mutation that creates it and fix there
Fix in the shared upstream service that every surface reads, not one edge mapper
If a check fails on canonical data, fix the check, not the data

L-never-executed-before-handoff.name: Script, query, command or write path handed over without running it once
L-never-executed-before-handoff.mechanism: New helper scripts, rewritten request builders, PySpark write paths, Dockerfiles and AWS commands are delivered after reading-only review. The first real run fails on an unhandled input variant, a nonexistent method, a missing package or unverified cluster config, and each fix surfaces the next failure through a slow pipeline.
trigger_signals: a new script or command for the user to run against real resources
a changed write path, request builder or Dockerfile with no test exercising it
PySpark code written without a SparkSession run
preventive_checks: Run it once against one real input (or a local build/docker build) before handing over
Diff the produced request/output against the pre-change version
For commands against prod resources, verify referenced config (capacity providers, revisions) with a read call first

L-llm-call-params-unsized.name: LLM call parameters not sized to reasoning, items per call or task type
L-llm-call-params-unsized.mechanism: max_tokens stays fixed while reasoning effort or items per request grow, reasoning tokens count against max_tokens without being returned, and creative default temperature is used for strict JSON extraction. Outputs truncate or vary, and validation failures look like model quality problems.
trigger_signals: changing reasoning_effort, model, or batching N items into one call
a structured/JSON extraction task with default sampling params
preventive_checks: Set max_tokens >= reasoning budget + worst-case output per item x items
Check finish_reason/truncation counts on a sample run
Use temperature 0 (or low) for deterministic extraction

L-derived-metric-wrong-denominator.name: Cost or rate metric computed with the wrong denominator, tier or components
L-derived-metric-wrong-denominator.mechanism: Per-unit costs and rates are derived from totals that include unrelated spend (evaluator cost), divided by a proxy count, labelled with a pricing tier the formula doesn't apply, or copy a per-request aggregate onto every exploded row. The number looks reasonable and drives a decision.
trigger_signals: estimating prod cost from a benchmark or bill
a column name that claims a tier/unit the formula must honor
exploding a batched response that carries a per-request usage field
preventive_checks: Write the formula with numerator and denominator sources named, and recompute from stored inputs
Exclude benchmark-only components from prod extrapolations
Divide per-request aggregates across exploded rows or keep them at request grain

L-non-idempotent-retried-step.name: Step run under retries or reruns is not idempotent
L-non-idempotent-retried-step.mechanism: Airflow retries, SQS redrive and same-day reruns re-execute steps that create DDL, emit terminal-failure events, append without dedup, or overwrite fixed keys from mutated inputs. The second attempt fails or duplicates side effects.
trigger_signals: a task with retries running CREATE/append/notify
an SQS handler that emits failure events and relies on redrive
a request to remove a dedup guard from a retried job
preventive_checks: Make DDL IF NOT EXISTS / CREATE OR REPLACE and writes MERGE or overwrite-by-partition
Emit terminal-failure side effects only on the final attempt
Flag retry semantics before removing an idempotency guard

L-integration-declared-unavailable.name: Integration or tool declared unavailable without discovering configured tools
L-integration-declared-unavailable.mechanism: Given a Slack/Notion/Linear link or a research task, the agent checks only its static tool list, tries a web fetch or browser automation, or dispatches a subagent type that lacks the needed tools, then stops or degrades instead of discovering the configured MCP namespaces.
trigger_signals: the prompt contains a Slack/Notion/Linear URL or asks to write to one
dispatching subagents for web research or external lookups
preventive_checks: Run the agent's dynamic tool/MCP discovery for the matching namespace before declaring anything unavailable
Prefer MCP tools over browser automation
Check the subagent type's tool set before delegating work that needs it

list-aggregate-endpoint.title: Add, change or optimize a list / aggregate / dashboard / tree read endpoint
list-aggregate-endpoint.description: Read-side API work: list or detail serializers with per-row fields, counts/sums/rollups, dashboard metrics, new filter dimensions on a scoped list, tree/hierarchy payloads, and query-count or perf tuning of those reads.

write-endpoint.title: Add or change a create / update / bulk write endpoint or service method
write-endpoint.description: Write-side API work: create/PATCH/upsert handlers, bulk or batch variants of a single-row action, sync/apply services, error-to-HTTP mapping, and read-after-write paths.

tenant-scoped-ids.title: Add an endpoint or route that resolves client-supplied ids (tenant scoping)
tenant-scoped-ids.description: Any view, nested sub-route, relation/linking endpoint, move/reparent or list-of-ids write that accepts an id from the client and must resolve it inside the caller's workspace/org/location scope.

permissions-auth.title: Change permissions, roles, RBAC codenames or auth / session gating
permissions-auth.description: Adding or narrowing a permission gate, changing a role's codename set, RLS policies, login/session/token-mint endpoints, permission-gated UI, and the tests that enforce them.

untrusted-input-validation.title: Accept or parse untrusted input (bot / LLM payload, CSV, HTML, client JSON)
untrusted-input-validation.description: Serializer validators or parsers that ingest client, bot, CSV, HTML or free-form input: type guards, bounds, max_length, sanitization, date sanity checks.

third-party-integration.title: Integrate a third-party API, SDK, webhook or platform
third-party-integration.description: Building or changing a client for an external system (chat platform, email/SMS provider, payment rail, HR system, AI vendor): pagination, idempotency, None bodies, trigger conditions, per-entity vs bulk calls, revoke flows.

side-effects-async.title: Add a background task, notification, outbox, alert or cache invalidation tied to a write
side-effects-async.description: Side effects that must be ordered against a DB commit or delivery outcome: cache deletes, provisioning chains, notification/email sends, outbox dispatch paths, sent-ledgers and alerting.

schema-model-change.title: Add or change a model, field, constraint, soft-delete behavior or schema migration
schema-model-change.description: Schema-level work: new models or fields, NOT NULL/defaults on a shared DB, uniqueness constraints, soft-delete managers, cascade/restore on self-referential trees.

state-transition-guard.title: Add or change a status transition, workflow state, lock or guard
state-transition-guard.description: State machines and guards: allowed-transition tables, blocked/paused flags, undo/retry windows, review locks, status-gated actions spanning several enum values, concurrency locks.

merge-clone-dedup.title: Write a merge, dedup, clone or copy routine over related records
merge-clone-dedup.description: Routines that combine, duplicate or re-identify records: user/account merges, org clone engines, merge-candidate detection, dedup heuristics, rename/merge sweeps and the FKs they repoint.

seed-import-backfill.title: Write a seed, import, fixture or backfill script / data migration
seed-import-backfill.description: Scripts and data migrations that populate or transform rows: seed/demo commands, external-system imports (Jira), backfills, delete-then-recreate migrations, create-or-reuse scripts.

live-data-fix-reconcile.title: Run a data fix, reconcile, rebuild or audit against live prod / staging data
live-data-fix-reconcile.description: Operating on real data: one-off cleanup or bulk delete scripts, balance-sheet reconcile and day rebuilds, drift/violation scanners, audit reports over many locations, manage.py against prod.

llm-extraction-pipeline.title: Build or run an LLM / OCR document extraction pipeline or agent callback
llm-extraction-pipeline.description: Agentic document pipelines: rasterizing PDFs, OCR/vision reads, barcode decoding, LLM-authored callback payloads, reconciliation gates before apply, retry/timeout loops.

fe-styling-layout.title: Style or lay out UI: CSS, theming, dark mode, responsive, print, formatting
fe-styling-layout.description: Visual work: CSS cascade and shared classes, dark-mode tokens, overlays' stacking, master-detail layouts, hand-rolled CSS geometry, print/PDF layouts, number/date display formatting.

full-stack-contract.title: Wire a feature across tiers (FE / API / worker): shared fields, params, enums
full-stack-contract.description: Cross-tier work where producer and consumer must agree: payload field names, list filter params, response shapes, duplicated business rules, UI built for backend capability (or vice versa), markup through sanitizers.

refactor-rename-shared.title: Refactor, rename or bulk-replace a shared symbol, component, type, label or format
refactor-rename-shared.description: Changes to something many callers depend on: renaming exports, redesigning a shared component's DOM, adding required fields to shared types, copy/format swaps, extracting modules - and the tests/drivers/mocks that assert the old shape.

write-e2e-spec.title: Write or extend a Playwright e2e spec, driver or proof screenshot
write-e2e-spec.description: Browser test authoring: locators and testids, driver classes, persistence assertions, stubbed responses and timing, seeded data dependencies, proof screenshots.

write-unit-tests.title: Write or change unit / integration tests (pytest, vitest)
write-unit-tests.description: Backend and FE unit/integration tests: fixtures that reach the branch under test, independent expected values, mocks that match the real call, suite isolation, benchmark cases.

run-local-verification.title: Run the app, dev server, tests or e2e stack locally to verify a change
run-local-verification.description: Standing up or reusing a local environment for verification: dev servers and autoreload, shared ports/DBs between sessions, health checks, host/IPv6/CORS bindings, test DB lifecycle.

triage-failure.title: Debug a failure or triage red tests to a root cause
triage-failure.description: Diagnosing: attributing red tests to the diff vs a pre-existing baseline, confirming root causes with direct evidence, reproducing reported bugs.

start-work-branch.title: Start or resume work on a branch or worktree (sync base, check existing work)
start-work-branch.description: The opening move of a task: choosing an isolated worktree vs the shared checkout, syncing with the latest base, checking whether the work already exists elsewhere, provisioning deps in a fresh worktree.

dispatch-parallel-agents.title: Dispatch, monitor or resume parallel agents, subagents or worktrees
dispatch-parallel-agents.description: Orchestration: fanning work out to agents/worktrees, allocating shared ids and files, pinning base SHAs, liveness checks on background agents, resuming vs re-dispatching, cleanup.

commit-push.title: Commit and push changes (hooks, staged files, push automation)
commit-push.description: Getting work into git: pre-commit/commit-msg hooks, repo size and style rules caught at commit, staging only this session's files, pushes that are expected to trigger automerge/CI.

merge-promote-branch.title: Merge, rebase or promote a branch (integration branches, conflicts, PRs)
merge-promote-branch.description: Moving work between branches: merging or rebasing onto a moved base, promotion hops (feature to dev/test/staging/main), migration-graph collisions, phantom conflicts, reverts and cherry-picks on shared branches.

deploy-release.title: Deploy or release the web / backend to staging or prod
deploy-release.description: Running or changing a deploy: deploy scripts and CI deploy workflows, where the build happens, what the pipeline carries, which checkout it deploys from, and checking the environment actually serves the change.

env-server-config.title: Change env vars, settings, secrets or live server / container config
env-server-config.description: Configuring where code runs: settings that read env/.env files or secret stores, host-dependent URLs and addresses, live service config (Postgres, nginx, systemd), containers/clusters, SSH sessions and cloud CLI credentials on remote boxes.

ci-pipeline.title: Change a CI workflow, test gate or build pipeline
ci-pipeline.description: CI configuration: what jobs actually run, sharding and result aggregation, pipefail, queued pipelines, schema/cache snapshots, secret scanning, typecheck coverage.

shell-scripting.title: Run shell commands or write a shell / CLI script
shell-scripting.description: Shell mechanics: exit codes through pipes, pkill/pgrep self-matches, cwd and relative paths, quoting and word-splitting, bash versions, inline code in commands, gitignore/pathspec semantics.

wrap-up-report.title: Wrap up: report done / pushed / deployed, or write docs and claims
wrap-up-report.description: Closing a task and anything that asserts facts: done/deployed reports, TDD evidence, build checks before claiming green, reference docs and commit prose that cite other artifacts, follow-ups for held-back fixes.

plan-scope.title: Plan or scope work from a requirement, mockup or reference UI
plan-scope.description: Before building: enumerating the full scope, resolving ambiguous terms or targets by asking, matching a mockup/reference product, modelling unusual personas (review/demo accounts).

tooling-dependency.title: Add or upgrade a dependency, or change dev tooling, hooks or agent memory
tooling-dependency.description: Toolchain changes: adding/removing packages and transitive deps, major tool bumps, git/agent hooks, interpreter pinning, shared memory/config files, heavy local tooling jobs.

concurrent-write-locking.title: Add or change row locking / concurrent write paths (lock order, select_for_update, advisory locks)
concurrent-write-locking.description: Any write path that takes row, parent-row, counter or advisory locks, or that must stay correct under concurrent requests, workers or bot callbacks: adding a lock, reordering locks, or adding a new operation to an entity family that other paths already lock.

document-parser-import.title: Build or change a document parser / converter / importer (HTML, Word, Markdown, transcript to blocks; re-index or align versions)
document-parser-import.description: Turning uploaded or converted documents into structured sections/blocks, re-aligning a new version against an old one, or extracting speakers/labels from text; the work is heuristic and must hold across real documents, not one sample.
